;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[May 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
**A [[truck bomb]] explodes near a [[court]] in [[Gardez]], [[Paktia Province|Paktia]], [[Afghanistan]], killing five civilians. The [[Taliban]] claims responsibility, calling it a retaliation to statements by [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] blaming the group for an attack on a maternity hospital two days ago. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attacks-blast/truck-bomb-in-eastern-afghan-city-kills-five-taliban-claim-responsibility-idUSKBN22Q0NY (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**The [[government of Mozambique]] announces that 50 Islamist [[insurgent]]s have been killed in recent operations in [[Cabo Delgado Province]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mozambique-insurgency/mozambique-government-kill-50-insurgents-in-recent-days-minister-idUSKBN22Q3CH?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[NATO]] [[Secretary General of NATO|Secretary General]] [[Jens Stoltenberg]] says the [[military alliance]] is "ready to support" the [[United Nations|UN]]-recognized [[Government of National Accord]]. [https://www.libyaobserver.ly/news/nato-ready-support-gna-libya-blocs-chief-says (''Libya Observer'')]
**[[Greece]], a member state of NATO, strongly criticizes Stoltenberg's remarks, saying his recognition of the "[[Muslim Brotherhood ]] government" does not reflect the positions of the military alliance. [https://greece.greekreporter.com/2020/05/15/greece-sharply-rebukes-nato-secretary-generals-support-of-muslim-brotherhood-in-libya/ (Greek Reporter)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**An [[Colombian Air Force|air force]] raid kills a senior [[National Liberation Army (Colombia)|National Liberation Army]] (ELN) commander and three others in a rural area of [[Bolívar Department|Bolívar]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-colombia-rebels/colombia-bombing-kills-eln-rebel-commander-three-others-idUKKBN22Q3G8?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Gunmen opened fire against two social workers delivering aid for people amid the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey|COVID-19 pandemic]] in [[Van Province]], [[Turkey]], killing them at the scene. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-05/15/c_139057722.htm (Xinhua)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Holy See|The Vatican]] announces that [[Pope Francis]] is sending a donation to [[Lebanon]] for 400 scholarships in an expression of his concern for the country’s young people. Lebanon is experiencing a “severe crisis” that is robbing younger generations of hope. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/pope-francis-supports-scholarships-in-lebanon-as-country-faces-severe-crisis-92971 (Catholic News Agency)]

;Business and economy
*[[Equinor]], a multinational [[oil company]] two-thirds owned by the [[government of Norway]], rejected a group of environmental and [[climate change]]-related resolutions at its [[shareholder]]s meeting. One of these called on Equinor to stop [[oil exploration]] in ecologically sensitive areas. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-equinor-climatechange-agm/equinors-shareholders-reject-climate-proposals-from-activists-idUSKBN22Q342 (Reuters)]
*The [[New York Stock Exchange]] is expected to partially reopen following [[Memorial Day]]. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/rachelsandler/2020/05/14/new-york-stock-exchange-will-partially-reopen-after-memorial-day/#2840de69f6ac (''Forbes'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[2020 Pacific typhoon season#Typhoon Vongfong (Ambo)|Typhoon Vongfong]] makes landfall in the [[Philippines]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/05/14/weather/typhoon-vongfong-philippines-landfall-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[Sheffield Cathedral|Cathedral Church of St Peter and St Paul]] in [[Sheffield]], [[England]], suffers damage due to a fire. There were no injuries. A 40-year-old woman has been arrested and charged with arson, burglary and assault of an emergency worker. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-south-yorkshire-52691116 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey]]
****[[Governor of New Jersey|Governor]] [[Phil Murphy]] announces that their beaches will reopen for Memorial Day, but with restrictions. [https://www.politico.com/states/new-jersey/story/2020/05/14/murphy-beaches-to-open-for-memorial-day-1284061 (''Politico'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Yemen]]
***[[Save the Children]] reports a surge in deaths of people with [[Coronavirus disease 2019|coronavirus]]-like symptoms in [[Aden]], with at least 380 in the last week. Officially, Yemen has only reported 13 COVID-19 deaths. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-52669301 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
***[[China]] marks a month without announcing new deaths. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/asia-today-china-marks-month-confirmed-deaths-70694726 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Seychelles]]
***The [[Seychelles]] bans [[cruise ship]]s until the end of [[2021]] effective immediately, amid fears over COVID-19. [https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/05/14/856417335/seychelles-bans-cruise-ships-until-2022-out-of-coronavirus-fears?t=1589553827328 (NPR)]

;International relations
*[[China–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] unanimously passes a bill placing visa and property sanctions on Chinese officials involved in [[Persecution of Muslims#China|the persecution]] of [[Uyghurs|Uyghur]] [[Islam in China|Muslims]] in [[Xinjiang]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/05/senate-approves-bill-sanction-china-uighur-rights-200515043805358.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Burundi]]
**[[Burundi]] expels the country's top [[World Health Organization]] representative and three other experts coordinating the [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] response. The [[Government of Burundi|government]] says they are ''[[persona non grata]]'' and must leave Burundi. They accused them of "interfering with the government response to the pandemic". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/05/burundi-expels-officials-coordinating-coronavirus-response-200514081736704.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Science and technology
*[[UFO sightings in the United States]]
**The [[United States Navy]]'s [[Naval Safety Center]] discloses "hazard reports" of Navy pilot encounters with [[Unidentified flying object|unidentified aerial phenomena]], including an incident in March 2014, in which a fighter jet pilot encountered an "unknown aircraft", which was "approximately the size of a [[suitcase]], and silver in colour." [https://news.sky.com/story/new-us-documents-reveal-more-details-on-ufo-encounters-11987977 (Sky News)]
